superseded_by: tests/fixtures/book_baseline_card144.json — CARD-144 deliberately changed what a book puzzle page prints (its frame — the owner's decision of 2026-09-23, intake at meta/architecture/inputs/raw-requirements.md:265, not yet a formalised requirement — closes the drawing off with one heavy rectangle), so interior 5 and interior 7, this book's two single-puzzle pages, moved. That is the one reason a successor may be recorded, and it was, under that card's number. Nothing below was regenerated: the other nine digests here are the ones CARD-144's recording carries too, and tests/helpers/book_corpus.BASELINE_FIXTURE now points at that file.
recorded_from_commit_note: This card's own implementation commit — the tree these digests were taken from, and the first one that reproduces them. The merge base (346d89e) writes an 8-page interior for the same book, so it cannot.
read_back_through: tests.helpers.pdf_pages.pdf_pages — the pages decoded out of the exported interior PDF, not the in-memory bitmaps
why_a_new_baseline: CARD-128 deliberately changes what the interior holds, which is the one reason the CARD-145 fixture's warning allows a new baseline to be recorded: the book now prints grouped easy, then medium, then hard (INV-009) and opens each non-empty level with a divider page (TERM-031), so this four-puzzle book's interior went from 8 pages to 11 and every page after the guide moved. The CARD-145 fixture is left in place, unregenerated, as the evidence it was recorded to be.
warning: This is evidence of what the book PDF looks like as of CARD-128. It must NEVER be regenerated to make a test fail less: a digest that no longer matches means a page's ink changed, which is what G-1 forbids. If a later card deliberately changes a page's content, it records a NEW baseline in a commit of its own, with its own card number, and says so here.
font_fingerprint_note: The guide page and every divider page are lettered in the system's Arial when Pillow can find it and in Pillow's built-in face when it cannot, so those pages' pixels are machine-dependent. A machine whose fingerprint differs from this one cannot be compared against the digests of the pages named in font_dependent_pages.
font_dependent_pages_note: The 1-based interior pages whose pixels depend on the machine's own font: page 1 is the guide page (Arial at 48 and 28, load_default fallback), pages 2, 4 and 6 are the Easy, Medium and Hard level dividers and page 8 is the SOLUTIONS divider (Arial at 60). The other six are drawn in the bundled band face and Pillow's built-in clue face, so their digests are comparable on any machine and are compared even when font_fingerprint differs. interior_bytes is compared only when the fingerprint matches: those pages sit inside the same file, and a different face changes the length of their JPEG streams.
